claims.harm: premature unmerged libmultiprocess subtree PR included ahead of upstream merge causes CI lint failure
claims.quote: Also it looks like the subtree is based on https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/269, which is still open. So this PR should be draft.
claims.settled_by_quote: Subtree PR adding the max connections PR has been merged and added to core

claims.harm: missing upper bound check allows large connection limits to overflow integer FD reservation and crash on startup
claims.quote: I believe it would be worth to add an upper bound check too because large values flow into the int FD reservation and overflow it
claims.settled_by_quote: Changed this to 1 for the lower bound and added an upper bound check.

claims.harm: using colon as options separator conflicts with Windows filesystem paths containing drive letters
claims.quote: I do really think the ':' options separator should be replaced by ',' to avoid problems with windows paths
claims.settled_by_quote: Addressed. socket options now use a comma separator, updated the PR description as well

claims.harm: size_t underflow and int overflow in FD accounting arithmetic bypass validation or cause assert crashes on startup
claims.quote: size_t underflow lets the aggregate check pass... The node starts up with min_required_fds reduced by 2 instead of failing
claims.settled_by_quote: I took your suggestion and capped IPC connections at 1 << 20, applied the same limit during parsing, and changed the aggregate check to avoid unsigned underflow.

claims.harm: unix socket paths containing commas cannot be reliably parsed without an escaping mechanism
claims.quote: The current implementation will accept unix:path,backup.sock=1 as valid when it should fail with Unknown socket option 'backup.sock'.
claims.settled_by_quote: Updated to use the previous solution

claims.harm: resolved socket path is lost in listener logging and error messages, showing only the unexpanded argument
claims.quote: This regresses the listener log line: before: Listening for IPC requests on address unix:/home/vinicius/.bitcoin/regtest/node.sock after: Listening for IPC requests on address unix
claims.settled_by_quote: I changed listenAddress to update ListenAddress::address directly, so the resolved socket path is now available to both the log and bind error message.

support.reason: IPC is a pretty generic feature, so it seems useful to be able to set different limits for different purposes (like GUIs vs mining clients).
I think this approach seems more reasonable than https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34978, even though both can work and both make sense this seems cleaner.
The -ipcbind=<address>:max-connections=8 option can later be expanded to include a whitelist of interfaces / methods (like -rpcwhitelist), unix group name and chmod flags.

Limiting IPC connections per listener makes sense. Tested manually on macOS and Linux by exercising the limit over the socket with raw and real clients, checking per-address behavior with multiple listeners
This fixes a gap in descriptor accounting, and adds a helpful connection limiting feature, and is nicely implemented.
Still looks good! And better now with the feedback from other reviewers avoiding overflows and restoring the detailed listening log line.
Now supporting URL escaping for unambigous parsing.
Tested locally using socat/nc with max-connections=1 and 2 clients: the first one connected successfully, and the second one waited in the backlog to be accepted once the slot was freed.

result.notes: Initial assessment brought up to date: all objections regarding subtree separation, option parsing on Windows, integer overflow/underflow in FD accounting, comma handling in paths, and listener logging regression have been resolved.
